findings.title: Storage failure recorded as a legacy duration
findings.body: In Create (line 45) and Update (line 129), a failure of the Storage call is recorded with recordLegacyDuration. The call that failed is the unified-storage one, so storage error metrics are missed and legacy error metrics are inflated. Both should use recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The goroutine that calls Legacy.DeleteCollection records its result with recordStorageDuration. That should be recordLegacyDuration. As written, the legacy outcome is counted under storage and the legacy metric is never emitted for this method.

findings.title: Delete uses d.Log instead of the enriched logger
findings.body: ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) discards the `log` built just above with name, kind and method values. Downstream log lines therefore lack that context. It should be klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

findings.title: Delete success metric labelled with name instead of kind
findings.body: The success path passes `name` (the object name) where every other call passes options.Kind. This creates one metric label value per object, which is a high-cardinality leak, and splits the series from the error path.

findings.title: Async legacy write reuses request context and objInfo after the request returns
findings.body: The goroutines derive their context from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the HTTP request finishes. The legacy write can then be cancelled before it runs. In Update, objInfo is also reused after Storage.Update has already applied it, and it is not rebased on the stored result. Create and Update also reuse the same obj or objInfo, which the storage layer may have mutated, so this can race and send inconsistent data to legacy. The goroutine should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and a copy of the stored result.

findings.title: Tests do not verify async legacy writes and can race with mock use
findings.body: The tests never wait for or assert the goroutine's legacy call. In the error-case Create test, setupLegacyFn registers a legacy mock, but Create returns before it is used. The unsynchronised testify mock is shared between the goroutine and the test, which can trigger the race detector or panics for unexpected calls. The Update/Create legacy calls therefore have no real coverage.
